counterfactual_missing_items: Ophthalmologic examination showed no evidence of retinitis
CT scan of the chest shows bronchiectasis with no consolidations or ground-glass opacities
decisive_items: Viral resistance testing showed mutations in UL97 (C592G) and UL54 (N408K) genes
Serial CMV viral load measurements:  * 63 IU/mL (1 month after initial treatment)  * 1089 IU/mL  * 321 IU/mL  * 340 IU/mL  * 660 IU/mL  * 1660 IU/mL and 3171 IU/mL (during hospital admission)
response.rationale: C1 is the most complete diagnosis: the UL97/UL54 resistance mutations and rising serial CMV viral loads despite treatment directly support drug-resistant CMV infection. R5 captures CMV infection but omits the drug-resistance subtype and temporal evolution. Other candidates are historical findings, prophylaxis-related, or lack specific CMV resistance evidence.

rejected.why: Chronic bronchiectasis is a pre-existing imaging/history finding and does not explain CMV viremia, resistance mutations, fevers, edema, or penile ulceration.
PCP is unsupported; the patient was on prophylaxis and CT showed no consolidations or ground-glass opacities.
MAC infection is historical only, with no active microbiologic or imaging evidence; it does not account for CMV resistance mutations.
IRIS is speculative; low CD4 and undetectable HIV viral load alone do not explain the specific CMV UL97/UL54 resistance mutations and rising CMV viral load.
